title: Where must the missing dot go to make the mean nine?
description: A dot plot shows ten dots and a mean of nine, but one dot is missing. The video works out the total the data must have, subtracts the total of the dots shown, and checks the answer by balancing the distances on both sides of nine.
teaching_notes: One idea: the total must equal the mean times the count, so the missing value is the needed total minus the shown total. Watch for students who put the missing dot at the mean, or who divide by ten instead of eleven.

source: Figure it Out (mean and median, question 2)
video_script.why: The child knows the mean and ten of the eleven values, and must find the one that is missing.
video_script.substitution: Find the total the mean needs, take away the total of the dots shown, and check that the distances balance.
video_script.anchor: a dot plot with ten dots on a number line, a mean marker at nine, and an empty slot for the missing dot
video_script.payoff_line: The missing dot is at sixteen

final_answer.spoken: the missing dot is at sixteen

hold_back: Answer: The missing dot is at 16
never_show: a dot at 9 marked as the missing dot
maths_rules: dots shown: 4, 7, 8, 8, 9, 9, 9, 9, 9, 11; that is 10 dots; with the missing dot 11 values
check: below 9 the distances are 5 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 9; above 9 they are 2 + 7 = 9
video_script.design: One idea: needed total minus shown total. The dot plot stays from ground to the end of the idea part.

narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>We use the same way as the example in your book. The missing dot makes eleven values in all.

narration: <bookmark mark='total'/>Step two, the needed total. The mean multiplied by the count is nine times eleven, which is ninety nine.
